title: Exposure of registration and device-enrollment data to unauthorized parties
description: During account registration and camera/sensor enrollment, the Home Hub receives personal identifiers, account credentials or contact details, and device identifiers/metadata. If the flow is not adequately protected, an attacker or unintended recipient could observe or obtain this information, revealing the homeowner's identity and details about devices installed in the home.
assumptions: The registration/enrollment flow carries personal data and device metadata over a channel that could be observed by unauthorized parties if not properly protected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the catalog distinguishes data-in-transit disclosure from broader unauthorized access.

title: Linkability of homeowner identity with enrolled device identifiers
description: The Home Hub can associate the homeowner's account registration data with unique camera and sensor identifiers submitted during enrollment. This may enable linking a specific person or household to a persistent set of devices across sessions, services, or datasets.
assumptions: Device serial numbers, MAC addresses, model identifiers, or similar persistent identifiers are collected during enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers.

title: Identifiability of the homeowner from registration attributes
description: Registration data such as name, email address, phone number, postal address, or payment/account details can directly identify the homeowner. Even if direct identifiers are minimized, combinations of attributes and enrolled device details may still make the homeowner identifiable.
assumptions: The registration process collects direct or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct or indirect identifiability from submitted attributes.

title: Detectability of home security system ownership or setup activity
description: Observing this flow may reveal that a person is registering a home-security account or enrolling cameras/sensors, thereby disclosing the existence of a monitoring system or the timing of installation/setup. Even without reading full contents, traffic patterns or protocol metadata may make this detectable.
assumptions: An observer can see the existence, timing, size, or destination of the communication.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; detectability trees often distinguish content-independent observability from explicit status disclosure.

title: Excessive collection of personal and device data during registration and enrollment
description: The Home Hub may request or accept more personal information and device metadata than is necessary to create the account and enroll devices, such as unnecessary profile fields, precise location, or extensive device telemetry. This creates a risk of non-compliance with data minimization and purpose limitation principles.
assumptions: The system design may collect optional or unnecessary fields beyond what is strictly needed for onboarding.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to over-collection; exact subtree naming may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Insufficient evidence or transparency about homeowner consent for device enrollment
description: If the system does not record clear proof that the homeowner initiated account registration and consented to enrolling each camera/sensor, the homeowner may later be unable to demonstrate what was authorized, or the provider may be unable to prove valid consent and enrollment actions.
assumptions: Enrollment may have legal or policy significance and requires demonstrable user action or consent records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation/consent logging; exact node may differ depending on whether LINDDUN Pro separates action repudiation from consent repudiation.

title: Unawareness of what personal and device data are submitted during onboarding
description: The homeowner may not understand which personal details, device identifiers, network information, or future processing purposes are involved when registering and enrolling cameras/sensors. Poor notice or unclear UX can leave the user unaware of the privacy implications of onboarding.
assumptions: Privacy notices, just-in-time explanations, or enrollment prompts may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Temporary access code can identify a specific guest or visit
description: If the Home Hub receives a unique temporary access code per guest or per booking, the code value or its successful use can identify which guest is present or attempting entry.
assumptions: Temporary codes are unique or mapped to a guest, reservation, or household event.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identification is modeled via direct identifiers or unique credentials.

title: Entry attempt reveals guest presence and arrival time
description: Submitting the temporary access code to the Home Hub discloses that a guest is at the door at a specific time, enabling inference of presence, arrival patterns, or occupancy.
assumptions: The Home Hub logs or forwards code-entry events with timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for disclosure of observed behavior/event data.

title: Access code itself may be exposed in transit or processing
description: The temporary access code is privacy-sensitive authentication data. If exposed during entry handling, debugging, telemetry, or insecure transmission inside the hub ecosystem, unauthorized parties could learn the code and infer guest access rights.
assumptions: The code is handled in plaintext at some point or insufficiently protected in logs, memory, or onward communications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive input/credential data; exact subtree may differ.

title: Guest may be unable to deny having entered the code
description: If the Home Hub records the temporary code entry and associates it with a guest or booking, those records can later be used as evidence that the guest attempted or performed entry, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Audit logs retain code-entry events and can be linked to a person.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation arising from event logging.

title: Guest may be unaware that code entry is logged or linked to them
description: The guest may not understand that entering the temporary code causes the Home Hub to log timestamps, failed attempts, or identity-linked access events, preventing informed expectations about privacy impact.
assumptions: Notice at the point of entry is absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Processing of guest access-code data may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: The Home Hub may process the temporary code and related entry metadata for purposes beyond unlocking the door, such as analytics, profiling, or long-term retention, without a valid legal basis or compatible purpose.
assumptions: System behavior includes secondary use, excessive retention, or inadequate legal notice/consent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance; exact node depends on the compliance issue emphasized.

title: Event log enables linkage of household activity over time
description: A persistent local event log of motion, door, and other sensor events can be correlated across timestamps to link separate observations into detailed occupancy and behavior patterns for the same household or individuals.
assumptions: The log stores timestamps and device/event identifiers over multiple sessions or days, and entries remain accessible for later correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via correlation of records over time; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Sensor event history can identify residents' routines
description: Even without explicit names, recurring motion and door events in the local log may identify specific residents or households by their unique daily routines, presence patterns, and device usage signatures.
assumptions: The event history is sufficiently granular and retained long enough to reveal distinctive patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from quasi-identifying behavioral data.

title: Local event log discloses in-home activities and presence
description: The stored event stream reveals when people are home, moving between rooms, opening doors, or otherwise interacting with the environment, exposing sensitive private-life information if accessed by unauthorized parties or secondary users.
assumptions: The datastore can be accessed by local administrators, malware, physical attackers, or other components beyond the original purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for unauthorized access to stored personal data.

title: Inference from logged sensor events reveals sensitive habits
description: Combinations of motion, door, and sensor events can allow inference of sleep schedules, absences, religious practices, health-related routines, or intimate relationships, beyond the raw events explicitly stored.
assumptions: Multiple sensor types and timestamps are logged with enough fidelity to support behavioral inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure by inference; exact subtree id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Residents may be unable to deny actions inferred from logged events
description: Because the Home Hub writes sensor-triggered events into a persistent log, those records may later be used as evidence that a resident entered, moved, or was present at a certain time, limiting plausible deniability even though sensor observations can be imperfect.
assumptions: The log is treated as authoritative by operators, household members, or investigators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation arising from persistent event records rather than explicit signatures.

title: Logging may occur without residents' awareness
description: Residents or visitors may not realize that the Home Hub persistently records motion, door, and sensor events to a local datastore, reducing transparency about ongoing monitoring inside the home.
assumptions: The system lacks clear indicators, notices, or accessible explanations of local logging behavior.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness about collection/storage; exact node id may vary.

title: Persistent local logging may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: Recording all motion, door, and sensor events to a local event log may go beyond what residents or visitors consented to, especially if retention, reuse, or access for troubleshooting, security, or household monitoring was not clearly agreed.
assumptions: Consent is absent, ambiguous, or limited to immediate device functionality rather than persistent storage and later analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/consent-purpose limitation concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Upload metadata can link clips to a specific household or device
description: When the Home Hub uploads recorded camera clips, identifiers such as device ID, account ID, IP address, timestamps, and clip naming conventions may allow the cloud service or other parties with access to correlate uploads over time and link them to the same home, occupants, and routines.
assumptions: The upload includes persistent identifiers or stable metadata and the cloud service can observe network and application-layer metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Stored video clips may reveal identities and sensitive in-home activities
description: Cloud video storage contains highly identifying content: faces, voices, visitors, possessions, room layouts, and behavioral patterns. If accessed beyond what is necessary, the clips can directly identify residents and expose intimate details of private life.
assumptions: Video clips are stored in a form accessible to the cloud provider or other authorized parties, or can be decrypted server-side.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from content itself; exact node id may vary in the LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Cloud storage enables profiling of household behavior from uploaded clips
description: Accumulated clips and their metadata can disclose occupancy schedules, sleep/work routines, frequent visitors, package deliveries, and other behavioral patterns. Even without watching every clip, timestamps, motion frequency, and retention history can reveal sensitive habits.
assumptions: The cloud service stores multiple clips over time together with timestamps and related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability/discoverability of sensitive patterns from stored observations; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that clips are uploaded to and retained in the cloud
description: Residents, guests, or passers-by may not realize recorded clips are transmitted off-device to cloud storage, how long they are retained, who can access them, or whether they are used for analytics or sharing. This reduces transparency about the existence and handling of personal data.
assumptions: Not all affected individuals are clearly informed about cloud upload, retention, and downstream access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency about data collection and storage; exact node id may differ.

title: Secondary use of uploaded clips may exceed the original home-security purpose
description: Once clips are stored in the cloud, they may be reused for service improvement, model training, law-enforcement response, employee review, or cross-product analytics beyond the user's expected purpose of storing security footage. Such repurposing can be incompatible with the original collection context.
assumptions: Policies, product settings, or operational practices permit uses beyond simple storage and user retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for use beyond intended/expected purpose; exact node id may differ.

title: Cloud retention and sharing practices may not comply with consent and data-minimization expectations
description: Uploading full video clips to cloud storage may conflict with privacy requirements if consent from residents or visitors is absent, retention is excessive, or collection is broader than necessary for the stated purpose. Cross-border storage or third-party access may further create compliance issues.
assumptions: Applicable legal or policy obligations require notice, consent, minimization, retention limits, or restrictions on third-party/cloud processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to consent, minimization, and retention; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of upload and handling can undermine accountability
description: If the Home Hub does not generate reliable logs or receipts for clip uploads, users may be unable to prove whether a clip was uploaded, when it was transmitted, or whether it was later altered or deleted in the cloud. This weakens accountability and can impede dispute resolution.
assumptions: Audit logging, integrity protection, or user-visible upload history may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation/accountability gaps around data transfer and storage; exact node id may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated motion alerts to the same household/device
description: Real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the backend may carry stable device, household, account, or network identifiers that allow the backend or anyone with access to backend-side telemetry to link multiple alerts over time to the same home and build a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The alert includes or is accompanied by persistent identifiers such as hub ID, account ID, certificate identity, or stable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Identifiability of residents from motion-alert metadata
description: Even if the payload is only a motion event, associated metadata such as precise timestamp, household identifier, installation address linkage, or user account context can make the alert attributable to a specific household or resident.
assumptions: Backend data can be associated with customer records, addresses, or user accounts.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Disclosure of occupancy patterns through stored or observable motion alerts
description: Motion alerts reveal when movement occurs in the home. If the backend stores, logs, exposes, or inadequately protects these alerts, an attacker or unauthorized insider could infer occupancy, routines, sleep patterns, or absence from home.
assumptions: Alerts are logged, retained, monitored, or otherwise accessible beyond the minimum necessary processing path.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Detectability of in-home activity from the existence or timing of alerts
description: The mere presence, frequency, or timing of transmissions from the Home Hub to the backend may allow an observer with network or backend visibility to detect that motion occurred, even without reading full payload contents.
assumptions: An observer can see traffic metadata, message arrival times, or event counters.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Unawareness of backend processing and retention of motion alerts
description: Residents may not understand that real-time motion alerts are forwarded to a backend, potentially retained, analyzed, correlated with account data, or used for secondary purposes beyond immediate notification delivery.
assumptions: Privacy notices, in-app disclosures, or setup flows do not fully explain backend-side processing of motion events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive collection or retention of motion-event data
description: Forwarding detailed real-time motion alerts to the backend may exceed data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or transparency requirements if more data than necessary is transmitted or retained longer than justified.
assumptions: The service stores detailed event histories or uses them for analytics, profiling, or other secondary purposes without an adequate legal basis or controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Repudiation gaps around receipt and handling of motion alerts
description: If the backend lacks privacy-preserving auditability, it may be difficult to prove whether a motion alert was received, forwarded, accessed, or deleted, undermining users' ability to contest processing or verify incident handling while also risking over-logging of personal data.
assumptions: Audit trails are incomplete, inaccurate, or not designed to support privacy rights and accountability.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than other categories; included because accountability for event handling can affect privacy. Exact node id may differ.

title: Notification content may disclose occupancy or in-home activity to unintended viewers
description: A motion-detected push notification can reveal that motion occurred at the home, which may expose presence patterns, occupancy status, or sensitive in-home activity if the notification is visible on a lock screen, shared device, or to someone with access to notification channels.
assumptions: The notification contains explicit text such as 'motion detected' and may be displayed on the phone lock screen or wearable companion devices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for message-content disclosure on a data flow may vary.

title: Repeated motion alerts can enable linkage of homeowner behavior patterns
description: Over time, motion-detected notifications sent from the backend to the homeowner can be correlated to infer routines such as when the homeowner is home, asleep, away, or moving through specific periods of the day. If notification metadata is observable by intermediaries or other apps, these events may be linked into a behavioral profile.
assumptions: An observer can access notification timing or metadata across multiple events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via repeated event correlation.

title: Notification delivery can reveal the homeowner's device endpoint or account association
description: Sending the push notification requires addressing a specific device token, account, or notification endpoint. Exposure or misuse of this addressing information could allow an observer or service provider to infer that a particular homeowner is associated with a specific home-security account or device.
assumptions: Push infrastructure or logs expose stable identifiers or routing metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact identifiability subtree may differ depending on whether focus is device token, account identifier, or routing metadata.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of notification visibility and metadata exposure
description: The homeowner may not understand that motion alerts can appear on lock screens, wearables, notification histories, or third-party push-service infrastructure, reducing transparency about who can see the alert and what metadata is exposed during delivery.
assumptions: The app does not clearly explain notification handling, preview settings, or third-party delivery implications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree may vary.

title: Motion notifications may be sent without valid or sufficiently granular consent/preferences
description: The backend may push motion-detected notifications even when the homeowner has not explicitly consented to this category of alert, has withdrawn consent, or expects finer-grained controls over content, timing, or recipients. This can violate user preferences and privacy expectations.
assumptions: Notification preferences or consent states may be absent, stale, or not enforced consistently by the backend.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance/consent-preference enforcement on this flow.

title: Insufficient evidence of notification delivery and preference enforcement can impede accountability
description: If the system does not keep appropriate records of when motion notifications were generated, what content was sent, and which user preferences or consent settings were applied, it may be difficult to later demonstrate whether the notification was sent appropriately or investigate privacy complaints.
assumptions: Audit logging for notification generation and policy evaluation is incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for accountability/repudiation-related privacy concerns; exact subtree may vary.

title: Analytics records may still be linkable to a device or user over time
description: Although the backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics, stable identifiers, small aggregation groups, timestamps, cohort keys, or repeated submissions can allow the vendor to link multiple analytics disclosures to the same device, account, household, or behavioral profile over time.
assumptions: The shared analytics may include persistent pseudonymous identifiers, fine-grained timestamps, or cohort dimensions that remain stable across uploads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of records across disclosures; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by catalog version.

title: Aggregated analytics may enable identification of individuals or devices
description: Even if data is described as aggregated, the vendor may be able to identify a specific user, device, or small group by combining rare usage patterns, sparse segments, metadata, or other datasets already available to the vendor.
assumptions: Aggregation may be over small populations or include dimensions that create uniqueness.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability/re-identification from received data.

title: Shared analytics may disclose sensitive behavior or attributes
description: Usage analytics can reveal app habits, routines, interests, location patterns, health-related behavior, or other sensitive inferences. The vendor may learn more than is necessary for the stated analytics purpose.
assumptions: The analytics include feature usage, event frequencies, timing, geography, or segmentation dimensions from which sensitive traits can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subnode may differ depending on whether the catalog distinguishes content disclosure from inference disclosure.

title: Users may be unaware that backend analytics are shared with a third-party vendor
description: Data subjects may not understand that their device-usage data, even in aggregated form, is transferred from the app backend to an external analytics provider, nor the scope of downstream analysis performed there.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-app disclosures may be incomplete, unclear, or not presented at the time of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Third-party analytics sharing may be incompatible with consent, purpose limitation, or minimization
description: Sending device-usage analytics to an external vendor may exceed the purposes originally communicated to users, rely on an invalid legal basis, or share more detail than necessary. Cross-border transfer, retention, or processor-controller role issues may also create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The vendor is a separate recipient and the transfer may not be fully covered by existing notices, contracts, or user choices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact subnode depends on the specific compliance obligation considered.

title: Vendor may lack sufficient information to support deletion or other data-subject rights
description: If analytics are aggregated or pseudonymized before transfer, the vendor may be unable to locate, delete, or export data relating to a particular user when rights requests are made, especially if mapping information is retained only by the backend.
assumptions: The vendor stores analytics in a form not readily attributable to a named individual, while still retaining enough utility to pose privacy risk.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for difficulties in intervenability/data-subject rights; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Excessive video retrieval exposes more personal footage than necessary
description: If the backend retrieves full-resolution or overly long stored clips from cloud storage when only a short segment or lower-quality preview is needed for playback, more personal data about residents, visitors, routines, and the home environment is disclosed within the system than necessary.
assumptions: The backend may request broader video content than is strictly needed for the homeowner's immediate playback request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for data minimization on internal retrieval may vary.

title: Backend can infer sensitive household behavior from retrieved video clips
description: By retrieving and processing stored video clips for playback, the backend can observe timestamps, motion patterns, occupants, visitors, and in-home activities, enabling inference of sensitive information such as presence at home, daily routines, relationships, or special-category data visible in footage.
assumptions: The backend has access to clip content and associated metadata during retrieval or streaming preparation.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for inference from content/metadata.

title: Retrieved clip metadata may enable linkage across sessions or devices
description: Identifiers attached to stored clips or retrieval requests, such as account IDs, device IDs, camera IDs, or clip IDs, may allow the backend or connected components to link multiple playback events and video records to the same household or user over time.
assumptions: Stable identifiers are used in storage and retrieval operations.
uncertainty_note: Exact linkage subtree may differ; node id is best-effort.

title: Playback retrieval may reveal the homeowner's surveillance habits
description: The act of requesting specific stored clips for playback can disclose that the homeowner is reviewing footage at particular times, potentially revealing concern about incidents, occupancy checks, travel status, or monitoring habits.
assumptions: Playback requests are observable within backend processing or logs and can be associated with a user or household.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure node; exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro.

title: User may be unaware that backend accesses full clip content during playback retrieval
description: Homeowners may assume playback is a direct fetch from storage, while in practice the backend may access, transform, cache, or inspect full video clips and metadata. This can undermine user awareness and informed expectations about how their footage is handled.
assumptions: System behavior is not fully transparent to users in notices or UI.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Retrieval and handling of stored video may exceed stated purpose or legal basis
description: If the backend retrieves stored clips for purposes beyond user-requested playback, such as analytics, model training, troubleshooting retention, or broad logging, the processing may be incompatible with the original purpose of collection or violate consent, contractual expectations, or data protection obligations.
assumptions: There is potential secondary use or insufficiently constrained processing once clips reach the backend.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort for non-compliance/purpose limitation concerns.

title: Insufficient evidence of authorized clip retrieval can hinder accountability
description: If retrievals from cloud video storage are not logged with sufficient integrity and context, the system may be unable to prove which stored clip was accessed, by whom, and under what authorization. This weakens accountability for privacy-relevant access to personal footage.
assumptions: Audit logging or tamper-evident records for storage reads may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation/accountability node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.
